title: Auto Loans: Starting Rate for an Autopay Enrollment
content:
The APR recorded when an Auto Loans account is enrolled in autopay is built from a starting rate that has every current discount taken back out. This note fixes that starting rate.

## Definition

The starting rate is the APR standing on the loan's record at the time of enrollment, increased by each discount that the loan's recorded discount list includes:

- if the list includes autopay, the autopay discount is restored;
- if the list includes relationship, the relationship discount is restored;
- the restored discounts, taken together, count for no more than the combined discount limit of the loan's product.

Discount sizes and the combined limit are those of the product the loan belongs to.

## Recorded list and amount restored

| The loan's recorded discount list | Restored to the recorded APR |
|---|---|
| none | nothing, so the starting rate equals the recorded APR |
| autopay | the autopay discount |
| relationship | the relationship discount |
| autopay and relationship together | their sum, or the combined limit if that is smaller |

## Illustration (made-up discount sizes, for arithmetic only)

A loan's record shows an APR of 7.00 and a discount list naming relationship only. If the relationship discount were 0.30, the starting rate would be 7.30. With a list reading none, the starting rate would stay at 7.00.
